newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electric futures seen mixed after May expiry.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electric futures seen mixed after May expiry.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures were called to open mixed Monday following expiration of the May contracts Friday.

In over-the-counter activity, June California-Oregon Border (COB) futures were quoted at $13.35-13.65 a megawatt hour (MWh) versus Friday's settlement at $13.31, while June Palo Verde (PV) was at $18.40-18.60 against Friday's close at $18.36.
Market sources said the complex could receive support by news that the shutdown of the 1,080 megawatt (MW) San Onofre nuclear unit 3 would be postponed to end-June from mid-June.
"The market did spike up late Friday on the San Onofre news," said one New York futures broker.
Southern California Edison Co announced it would extend the outage at unit, in San Clemente, California, for repairs at the unit's steam generators.
Some players said the complex would trend lower in line with weaker natural gas futures.
NYMEX June Henry Hub futures were down 3.1 cents at $2.095 per million British thermal units in early trading.
In the meantime, May COB paper prices were assessed at $14.25-14.60, lower than Friday's expiration at $14.71 and May PV at $17.95-18.40 compared with Friday's expiry at $18.20.

Near-term prospect for the Northwest power market was bolstered by talk that Bonneville Power Administration (BPA) will continue to limit its offer of daily surplus power well into May, market sources said.
Forecasters said temperatures in the Northwest would average near or slightly below normal through the rest of week with above normal precipitation.
In the Southwest, dry and very warm weather would settle over the southern part of the region with readings averaging six to 12 degrees Fahrenheit above normal.
Cloudy skies and seasonable temperatures were predicted for Utah, Colorado and northern California.
